blocks.content: Section 6 of the DSPE Act, 1946 mandates that the Delhi Special Police Establishment cannot exercise powers and jurisdiction in any area in a State without the consent of the Government of that State.

rows: Blanket approval granted by states for seamless investigation of corruption cases.
Case-by-case permission required prior to registering an investigation.
High efficiency; officers can conduct operations without prior administrative delay.
Lower efficiency; approval must be sought individually for each new case or officer.
Stops registration of fresh cases without explicit permission; pending cases continue unaffected.
Does not apply since consent is granted individually on a per-case basis.

items: Withdrawal of general consent by a state does not affect existing, previously registered CBI cases, nor does it restrict Supreme Court or High Court orders directing CBI inquiries.
Constitutional amendments amending federal provisions require state ratification by a SIMPLE majority, not a special majority in state legislatures.
Parliament can re-name, alter boundaries, or create new states under Article 3 even if the affected state legislature opposes the bill.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Section 6 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act, 1946 mandates State Government consent for CBI investigations within state jurisdiction.
General Consent permits the CBI to investigate corruption and crime seamlessly without seeking individual approvals for each case.
Withdrawal of General Consent forces the CBI to obtain specific case-by-case approval before registering fresh cases in that state.
Constitutional amendments affecting federal structures under Article 368 require ratification by at least 50% of state legislatures via simple majority.
Under Article 3, while the President refers state reorganization bills to state legislatures for views, state consent is not binding on Parliament.
